findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu, and init now calls it while the watch goroutine can be writing the map
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock (bleve.go:144-153). `BuildIndex` writes the map under `cacheMu.Lock()` (bleve.go:137-139). The new log line at search.go:216 calls `s.search.TotalDocs()` after the watch goroutine has already started (search.go:202-213). For every event, that goroutine calls `getOrCreateIndex`, and on a cache miss it runs `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache`. If an event for a namespace/resource with no index yet arrives right as init finishes, the map is iterated and written at the same moment. Go aborts the process with `concurrent map iteration and map write`, so storage startup crashes. The metrics collector (bleve_index_metrics.go:96) has the same unlocked read; until now it was the only caller. Fix: take `b.cacheMu.RLock()`/`RUnlock()` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: Parallel init workers share the outer `err` (and `totalBatchesIndexed`), and they now really do run in parallel
findings.body: Every `group.Go` closure assigns to the `err` declared at line 181 (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and then returns it. It also increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization (line 189). Before this PR, `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for the whole build, so the workers effectively ran one at a time. With the lock now taken only around the map write (bleve.go:137-139), `WorkerThreads` > 1 runs builds at the same time. One worker can overwrite another's non-nil `err` with nil between the assignment and the `return err`. `group.Wait()` then returns nil, and init reports success with an index missing; that index is only built later, on first lazy access. The span attribute count at line 199 also becomes unreliable. Fix: declare the error inside the closure (`_, _, err := s.build(...)`) and use an atomic counter or a mutex for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

findings.title: Postgres skip probably hides a test config bug that eager Init now exposes
findings.body: Before this PR, `server.Init` (and with it `backend.Init`, i.e. the DB connection) ran lazily on the first request, so this test passed without the storage server ever touching the resource DB. Now `NewResourceServer` calls `s.Init` (server.go:258), so `sql/service.go:113` connects at module start. For postgres, `addStorageServerToConfig` hardcodes `db_host = "localhost"` (line 76). The mysql branch's comment (line 81) says localhost does not work in Drone, and that branch parses the host from the connection string. That fits "fails in Drone, works locally". Parsing the postgres host from `connection_string` the same way would likely let the test run again instead of being skipped.

findings.title: Stop's `initErr` no longer blocks requests after shutdown
findings.body: `Stop` still sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped" (lines 321, 328, 339). Before, those values reached clients because every handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr`. Now that those calls are gone, nothing reads `initErr` after construction. After `Stop`, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Search, and `IsHealthy` (which feeds the gRPC health service, health.go:35), keep being served as normal, and the writes to `initErr` are dead. If refusing requests after shutdown matters, add an explicit stopped check (e.g. an atomic flag) to the handlers or at least to `IsHealthy`. Otherwise, remove the `initErr` writes in `Stop`.

findings.title: Init failure is logged twice, and the server context is not cancelled on that path
findings.body: `Init` already logs "error initializing resource server" (line 314), and `NewResourceServer` logs the same message again (line 260). On this error path the constructor also returns without calling `s.cancel()` for the context made at line 229. If `initWatcher` fails after `search.init` succeeded, the search watch goroutine started at search.go:207 keeps running on `context.Background()`.

contracts.action: NewResourceServer now runs Init (lifecycle Init, search index build, then watcher) eagerly at construction; per-request Init calls are removed
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: each handler (Create/Read/List/Watch/Search/IsHealthy/blob) called s.Init(ctx) lazily on first request, with sync.Once guarding it
contracts.before_after: Before: Init errors surfaced as per-request errors and init ran with the first caller's ctx. After: Init runs with the server's background ctx carrying the 'watcher' service-account claims (server.go:229-235), and a failure makes the constructor return an error. Callers sql/server.go:77, client.go:67 and client.go:101 propagate the error, so startup fails. The watcher now starts after the search index is built (server.go:303-311).
contracts.visible_effect: Startup of the storage server/in-process client blocks until all indexes are built and the DB is reachable; misconfiguration now fails at start instead of on first request.
contracts.failure_mode: An Init error is returned from the constructor and logged twice; s.cancel is not called. Stop() still writes initErr, but nothing reads it any more, so requests after Stop are not rejected.

contracts.action: search init logs TotalDocs after starting the watch goroutine
contracts.before_after: Both call sites read b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex writes it under cacheMu
contracts.visible_effect: Log line with the duration and doc count
contracts.failure_mode: A concurrent map iteration and write with a handleEvent-triggered BuildIndex makes the Go runtime abort the process

contracts.action: bleve BuildIndex locks cacheMu only around the map write instead of for the whole build
contracts.before_after: Before, all builds were serialized. Now init workers (errgroup, limited to WorkerThreads) build in parallel, which exposes the shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in the init closures
contracts.failure_mode: Racing writes to `err` can swallow a build error, so init reports success

contracts.action: Spans now propagate ctx into children (GetResourceStats, search build/init)
contracts.equivalent_path: Other backend methods use ctx, span := b.tracer.Start
contracts.before_after: Child spans are now parented correctly; there is no functional change

summary: Init now runs eagerly in NewResourceServer, and the bleve cache lock moved off the whole build, so init builds indexes in parallel. That exposes two concurrency bugs. The new TotalDocs log line reads b.cache with no lock while the watch goroutine may be writing it, which can crash the process. And the parallel init workers share `err`, so one build's error can be overwritten and lost. Also: Stop's initErr no longer stops requests from being served after shutdown, and the new postgres test skip likely hides a hardcoded-localhost config bug that eager Init now exposes.
